chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of them (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about a man who had made it incumbent upon himself to walk to the House of God, but he was unable to do so; he said: 'He performs Hajj riding.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who vowed to walk to Mecca but cannot?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies that a vow to perform Hajj on foot is not binding if physical incapacity arises, allowing the devotee to fulfill the obligation by riding. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-yusr* (ease) in fulfilling vows, ensuring that the intent of the vow is preserved without imposing undue hardship. It highlights the flexibility within *Nudhur* (vows) where the mode of execution adapts to the vow-maker's actual capacity.
